name: FlowMatch Scheduler (ai-toolkit style, with random types)
plain: Multi-mode scheduler: linear, shift, shift_exponential, flux_shift with resolution μ, plus sigmoid and lognorm_blend types whose sigmas are random draws that get sorted. Those two types mirror training timestep sampling and change per run. Options add bell-curve weighting and terminal stretch.
math:
linear: linspace(1,0,n+1)[:-1].
sigmoid: σ=sorted(1−sigmoid(randn(n))).
lognorm_blend: α·n draws 1−X/max X (LogNormal) ∪ linspace; sorted.
shift: e^μ/(e^μ+(1/t−1)) or μt/(1+(μ−1)t).
bell: y=e^{−2((i−n/2)/n)²}; w=(y−min y)·n/Σ; σ×w/mean w.
terminal: stretched=term+(σ−σ_{−2})·(1−term)/(σ₀−σ_{−2}).
Then 0 (or 1 if inverted).

props.params: scheduler_type, shift, base_shift=0.5, max_shift=1.16, shift_terminal, use_bell_curve, lognorm_alpha=0.75, lognorm_scale=0.333

label: from code
surprise: The sigmoid and lognorm_blend types use unseeded torch.randn or LogNormal.sample, so an inference schedule varies per run; the bell-curve option multiplies sigmas directly and can break the descent before re-sorting (flowmatch_scheduler.py:233, 206).
